chapter: Learning trombone and the Wisconsin Roof years
title: Eli Rice, Arthur Sims and the Wisconsin Roof
summary: He toured with Eli Rice, then joined Arthur Sims at the Wisconsin Roof, where Albright and Bernie Young later led the band.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Yeah, yeah, Dutre taught me, Roy taught me more so. And then I, later on as I progressed, I joined Eli Rice's band. I stayed with him about 14 months. We traveled all through Wisconsin and Minnesota and Michigan, Michigan and Minnesota. And I used to get out there in them woods and practice. So after 14 months I came back to Chicago and I played the great pianist Teddy Weller for him at the Dream. And Shirley Clare was on the cornet myself and Teddy and I had forgotten the fellow who could play drum and sing very well. And I think Artis Starks was on there, Clownet and Sax. So we came back pain night and Padlock was on the police. I know 5250 was paying us. I knew we'd get that money. I just said married too. And so I, then I went and joined Arthur Sims in Milwaukee, Wisconsin Roof. And so after about a year, with Arthur, Arthur caught me in August and died. So then, the fellow who was now, is a physician. He, Arthur Albright, he was the oldest man in the band. He was a guitar player in the band, the band, the band of yours. And he taken over the band and he left to go to Mayharry to study medicine. That's what Oscar Bernie Young. Now he and I were schoolmates too, at the time we were from school. So, I had played with him in discipline called the Paramount. . . . .
I think Audis Starks was on there, Clamondon and Saxe.

So we came back, Pay Night and Padlock was on the place. I know 5250 was paying us. I didn't really get that money, I just said married to. And so then I went and joined Arthur Sims in Milwaukee at the Wisconsin Roof. And so after about a year with Arthur, Arthur caught pneumonia in August and died. So then a fellow who is now a physician, Arthur Albright, he was the oldest man in the band. He was a guitar player and banjoist. So he was taking over the band and then he left to go to Meharry to study medicine. That's when Oscar Burney Young, now he and I were schoolmates too, we had a time to come to school. So I had played with him in this record for Paramount, previous to that, before he ever joined Sims up in Wisconsin. And that's some of the stuff that's on this record now. I presume Buddy Young's on here. Yeah, he's on this record. Yeah, yeah. So we stayed there about close to six years. With Art Sims? Huh? With Art Sims? Yeah, not with Art Sims, because Art Sims died. But between the two leaders, Arthur Albright and Bernie Sims. And in this particular band we had Edward Inge, did you ever hear, he used to play with Don Redmond. He made that famous tune, Channel the Weed. And we had Cas No Simpsons, he was a great pianist. And we had Gilbert Mundy, Burt Bailey, those were saxophonists, Gilbert, Double on the Fiddler. We had three arrangers in the band. And we had Irvin, Miles Randolph, and Bernie on trumpet, and myself on trombone. But I could see my short, I could see rather that I wasn't right up to par. So I began to take some lessons in Milwaukee, the president of this white union there, see. I'd taken lessons in him about five, six months. And then we left there and we went to Savoy. And in fact we went to Indianapolis, the brother Tom's place up there, the Indiana roof, Indianapolis. This was the Wisconsin roof. So after two weeks when we came back we didn't have no job, probably by the name of Grant Moore. His band was in there and Grant Moore had a chicken train, he used to run across the stage, you know. A what?
